Suppose that <MATH_0001> has a section.
Then for any <MATH_0002>-module <MATH_0003> the extended cochain complex
(<REF_0001>) is exact.

By
Simplicial, Lemma <REF_0001>
the map <MATH_0001> is a homotopy equivalence
of cosimplicial <MATH_0002>-algebras
(here <MATH_0003> denotes the constant cosimplicial <MATH_0004>-algebra).
Hence <MATH_0005> is
a homotopy equivalence in the category of cosimplicial
<MATH_0006>-modules, because <MATH_0007> is a
functor from the category of <MATH_0008>-algebras to the category
of <MATH_0009>-modules, see
Simplicial, Lemma <REF_0002>.
This implies that the induced map of associated
complexes is a homotopy equivalence, see
Simplicial, Lemma <REF_0003>.
Since the complex associated to the constant cosimplicial
<MATH_0010>-module <MATH_0011> is the complex
<MATH_0012>
we win (since the extended version simply puts an extra <MATH_0013> at
the beginning).

Suppose that <MATH_0001> is faithfully flat, see
Algebra, Definition <REF_0001>.
Then for any <MATH_0002>-module <MATH_0003> the extended cochain complex
(<REF_0002>) is exact.

Suppose we can show there exists a faithfully flat ring map
<MATH_0001> such that the result holds for the ring map
<MATH_0002>. Then the result follows for
<MATH_0003>. Namely, for any <MATH_0004>-module <MATH_0005> the cosimplicial
module <MATH_0006> is
just the cosimplicial module <MATH_0007>.
Hence the vanishing of cohomology of the complex associated to
<MATH_0008> implies the
vanishing of the cohomology of the complex associated to
<MATH_0009> by faithful flatness of <MATH_0010>.
Similarly for the vanishing of cohomology groups in degrees
<MATH_0011> and <MATH_0012> of the extended complex (proof omitted).
